first_handback:
I read all 90 files, one `cat` call each and in order. The report has one table row per file, with file name, station name, founding year and founder.

Report: /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/u-c1/lab/__reports__/wave-04/explorer-w04-uc1/00-findings_v0.md

Station names are not unique. The 90 files carry 58 distinct names, and 24 names recur with different founders and years. Quillhaven, for example, appears in f019 (1849, Dov Maro), f034 (1884, Cora Ashby) and f041 (1844, Dov Verrin). I kept every file as its own row and did not merge them. The files don't say whether these are separate stations that share a name or conflicting records.

- **Not tabulated:** elevation, population, occupation and wind-day fields, because the brief asked only for name, year and founder.
- **Transcription:** I typed the rows by hand from the `cat` output, with no script parsing the raw files, so a transcription error is possible. The distinct-name and repeated-name counts come from running `sort | uniq -c` on my transcribed `rows.txt`, not on the raw files.

The one puzzle is in /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/u-c1/lab/__scrupuli__/wave-04-explorer-w04-uc1.md. The transcribed rows are in /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/u-c1/lab/__reports__/wave-04/explorer-w04-uc1/rows.txt.
